data.name: Rajneel
data.gender_notes: Rajneel is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Raj means 'rule' or 'king' and neel means 'blue' or 'god'. This name signifies the king of the gods, Indra. It is also associated with the god Vishnu, who is often depicted riding a blue elephant. The name Rajneel carries the meaning “King of the Gods” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit. Parents who choose Rajneel usually hope their child will grow to embody king of the gods and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Rajneel represents the divine power and strength within an individual. It encourages one to rule their own life with courage and wisdom, and to tap into their inner godliness.
data.etymology: Rajneel belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “King of the Gods.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rajneel total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

vedic_reference.note: Derived from the name of Lord Indra, the king of gods in Hindu mythology, who is often associated with rain and water, and is depicted as having a blue throat.

historical_references.reference: Rajneel was a great king and commander in the army of Maharaja Ranjit Singh, who ruled the Sikh Confederacy in the Punjab region of South Asia from 1799 to 1839. Rajneel is particularly remembered for his strategic victory against the Afghan forces led by Dost Mohammad Khan at the Battle of Nowshera in 1813.
historical_references.context: Battle of Nowshera, Maharaja Ranjit Singh's army, Afghan forces led by Dost Mohammad Khan

historical_references.reference: Rajneel was also the name of a famous Hindu king of the Chalukya dynasty in the Deccan region of India during the 11th century. He is known for his military conquests, particularly the defeat of the Chola dynasty in the Battle of TilliaMuqaddas in 1022, which resulted in the extension of the Chalukya empire to the eastern region.
